headline: Synaptic tuning, sign constraints and conductance shape coding limits and network dynamics
label: Synaptic Constraints On Neural Coding
summary: Recent preprints treat synaptic tuning, sign constraints, and conductance as direct limits on population coding efficiency and dynamics.
synthesis: The three preprints treat synaptic-level properties as direct determinants of network coding limits rather than background. One analyzes optimal decoding under coarse-tuned synaptic weights and reports that decoder SNR saturates with population size under strong tuning. A spiking-network model with bilingual neurons that violate Dale's principle shows sync/async transitions differing from monolingual controls. A parameter-free biophysical model predicts that synapses operate at SNRs maximizing bits per Joule, consistent with an observed efficiency drop with conductance. The dominant thread is coupling synaptic parameters to population readout and to coding or dynamical outcomes. The first and third connect through information-theoretic limits, while the second addresses dynamical transitions, and the Dale's-principle item does not address coding efficiency directly. What is new is the explicit framing of synaptic structure as a constraint on coding efficiency and population-level computation.
